qt: to the Commission Elena Lizzi (ID) Subject:
Implementation of the strategy for the rights of persons with disabilities 2021-2030

In March 2021, with a view to improving the lives of persons with disabilities in Europe and around the world, the Commission adopted the strategy for the rights of persons with disabilities 2021-2030. The European Court of Auditors’ special report entitled ‘Supporting persons with disabilities’ explicitly states that, in practice, EU action is having a limited impact, highlighting that: — it is difficult to monitor funding with a view to determining whether it is improving the lives of persons with disabilities; — the Commission is struggling to compare information collected by the Member States because they use different information-gathering systems; — the EU institutions do not know exactly how many persons with disabilities they have hired. According to evidence presented by the Court of Auditors at the EMPL Committee hearing of 30 November 2023, Parliament is the only EU institution to have provided the Court of Auditors with information to that effect. In the light of the above: 1.
How many persons with disabilities are employed either by the Commission or by the EU agencies under its supervision?
Why has the Commission not shared this information with the European Court of Auditors?
What are its recruitment practices for hiring persons with disabilities?

(9 April 2024) As an employer, the Commission aims to lead by example in implementing the European Disability Strateg y (1) and takes actions to boost the recruitment, effective employment and career prospects of staff with disabilities in line with its new Human Resources Strategy (2). The Commission does not collect the data on its employees’ disabilities unless the employee concerned voluntarily provides it with this information. In addition, any data provided are subject to data protection rules. The Commission established a benchmark via a dedicated voluntary survey in 2021 on how staff members with disabilities perceive their inclusion (3). It then adopted a Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan for 2023-2024 (4). The Commission will repeat a similar survey at the end of the implementation period of the action plan. In all its recruitment channels the Commission refers to the principle of equal opportunities and invites all qualified candidates, including those with disabilities, to apply for open positions. The Commission, upon request, provides candidates with targeted support and assistance throughout the recruitment process, and raises awareness of recruitment panels on its equal opportunities policy.
